findings.problem: fs::read_to_string(path).unwrap() panics on any I/O failure (missing file, permissions, ENOMEM)
findings.failure_mode: untrusted or missing file path aborts the entire process with a panic instead of returning a typed error the caller can handle
findings.fix: return a Result<Vec<Record>, LoadError> and use .map_err(|e| LoadError::Io(e)) or use a fallible I/O abstraction

findings.problem: println!("loaded {}", parts[0]) fuses logging (side-effecting I/O) into a parsing/mapping closure that should be pure
findings.failure_mode: parsing logic has a hidden dependency on stdout; pure consumers of the mapping closure get observable side effects, breaking determinism and making the function impossible to test without capturing stdout
findings.fix: remove println! from the parsing closure; if metrics/logging are needed, surface them in the shell layer after parsing completes

findings.problem: parts[1].parse::<u32>().unwrap() panics when the CSV field is not a valid u32
findings.failure_mode: malformed CSV data (e.g. "foo,bar") causes a panic instead of a recoverable parse error
findings.fix: return Result and use .map_err(|_| ParseError::InvalidValue) on the parse call

findings.problem: (parts[1].parse::<u32>().unwrap() as u16) silently truncates any u32 value > 65535
findings.failure_mode: a valid u32 like 70000 becomes 4464 due to truncation, corrupting domain data without any error signal
findings.fix: use u16::try_from(value).map_err(|_| ParseError::Overflow) to reject out-of-range values with a typed error

findings.problem: parts[0] uses unchecked indexing on a Vec produced by split with no length guard
findings.failure_mode: an empty line or a line with no commas panics at runtime via index out of bounds
findings.fix: check parts.len() >= 2 before indexing, or use split_once and match on the (name, value) tuple

findings.problem: parts[1] uses unchecked indexing on a Vec produced by split with no length guard
findings.failure_mode: a line with only one comma-separated field panics at runtime via index out of bounds
findings.fix: require exactly two fields via split_once and match, eliminating indexing entirely

findings.problem: load_metrics fuses file I/O, logging, CSV parsing, numeric validation, and domain construction into a single impure function
findings.failure_mode: no separation between shell (I/O) and core (parsing/validation); makes the function untestable as pure logic, impossible to compose, and violates the Functional Core / Imperative Shell architecture
findings.fix: split into two functions: a pure fn parse_metrics(lines: &[&str]) -> Result<Vec<Record>, ParseError> for the core, and a shell fn load_metrics(path: &str) -> Result<Vec<Record>, LoadError> that handles I/O and delegates to parse

findings.problem: raw String values from CSV are used directly as Record fields without any smart constructor, validation, or bounded resource cap; the line also uses split(',').collect() instead of the mandatory split_once for one-separator grammars
findings.failure_mode: raw primitives cross the parse boundary without fallible smart constructors, so callers can construct invalid domain states; split(',').collect() also over-allocates into a Vec<String> instead of extracting the two fields directly
findings.fix: use line.split_once(',').ok_or(ParseError::Invalid) to extract (name, value_str), validate name is non-empty via a smart constructor, parse value_str with checked try_from<u16>, and add a max_records cap with try_reserve before collecting

findings.problem: load_metrics has no max_items/records cap and does not call try_reserve before collecting into Vec
findings.failure_mode: an attacker or malformed input file can trigger unbounded heap allocation (DoS) and the collect() into Vec allocates freely with no capacity hint
findings.fix: accept a max_records: usize parameter, validate it, call Vec::with_capacity or try_reserve capped by max_records, and return a TooMany error when exceeded

findings.problem: load_metrics returns Vec<Record> with no error type, making it impossible to distinguish I/O errors, parse failures, overflow, and allocation failures
findings.failure_mode: callers cannot recover from or report specific failure modes; all errors are either swallowed by unwrap or invisible due to non-Result return
findings.fix: define enum LoadError { Io(std::io::Error), Parse(ParseError), TooMany { max: usize }, Allocation(std::alloc::AllocError) } and return Result<Vec<Record>, LoadError>

residual_risk: This is a static-only review of a 23-line crate with 10 BLOCKER findings: multiple unwrap panic surfaces, unchecked indexing, lossy as cast, hidden I/O (println) in pure parsing logic, fused shell/core responsibilities, missing error taxonomy, unbounded allocation, raw primitive domain state without smart constructors, and split(',').collect() violating the mandatory split_once rule. No commands were run. The crate has no tests, benchmarks, or binaries. Every finding requires production source repair before any delivery or landing gate can pass.
